newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares advance strongly in early bourse.
newsitem.headline: German shares advance strongly in early bourse.

text.p: Germany's DAX index surged about two percent in early bourse dealings on Tuesday, getting a boost from overnight Wall Street gains and a firmer dollar.

Market conditions were favourable for additional gains, traders said, after the Bundesbank left its weekly securities repurchase agreement, or repo, fixed at three percent and signaled for now that German rates would not be raised.
The 30-share DAX index was up 85.11 points at 4,163.71 points in early bourse dealings. The IBIS DAX, which reflects all-day computer trade, was up 80.96 points at 4,161.51.
"The fact that the Bundesbank left the repo unchanged means there is no sign of a rate move," said one Frankfurt broker.
"Volumes are pretty thin at the moment, but I reckon that when they do come in to the market, they will be on the buy side," the broker said.
Luxury carmaker Porsche AG, whose shares have taken a beating as the dollar began sliding late last week, was among the top percentage gainers.
Preference shares in Porsche were up nearly 10 percent, rising 240 marks to 2,700 marks.
Volkswagen AG was also higher after reporting strong first-half results on Monday, rising 70 marks to 1,355 marks.
The Wolfsburg-based carmaker on Monday said group net profit rose 73 percent in the first six months of the year.

VW chief executive Ferdinand Piech also said in a television interview on Monday that VW expected a good 700,000 orders in Europe for its new Golf model, to be unveiled on Tuesday in Bonn, in the first year of production.

Bayer AG was up 1.30 marks at 71.30 marks after the chemicals and pharmaceuticals group said net profit for the first half of 1997 rose 13 percent to 1.7 billion marks along with an 11 percent rise in sales to 27.4 billion marks.
German banks shares were notably higher after also incurring heavy losses in the previous days.
Commerzbank AG, considered a prime takeover target in growing speculation for further industry mergers, was up four marks at 68 marks.
Deutsche Bank AG also gained, rising 3.55 marks to 114.65 marks, while Dresdner Bank AG was up 2.80 marks at 79.30 marks.
